title: Cîteaux (1098)
hookLine: monks seek a simpler, stricter Benedictine life in white habits

cards: An iron candlestick. A cross of painted wood, not gold. Walls of bare stone, and light coming in through plain glass.
Stand in an old Cistercian church and the first thing you may notice is what isn't there. No crowd of carved monsters on the columns. No silver on the altar.
Just stone, light, and the sound of a few voices singing psalms. The builders chose less, on purpose.

teach.h: CUT WHAT ISN'T IN THE RULE.
teach.b: Robert, abbot of a monastery called Molesme, came to think that he and his monks weren't keeping the Rule of Saint Benedict as it was written.
So he left with a group of brothers and founded what the early accounts simply call the New Monastery, in a wild, lonely place called Cîteaux.
Their own early account says they set aside whatever they couldn't find in the Rule: fur garments, undershirts, extra dishes at table.
They went back to working the land with their own hands, in habits of undyed wool, which is why people came to call them the white monks.
Early Cistercian rules ask for crosses of painted wood, not gold or silver, and candlesticks of iron. The aim wasn't ugliness. It was attention: nothing in the room competing with prayer.
One of the early abbots, Stephen Harding, is credited with a Charter of Charity linking the new houses, so they kept one way of life and looked after one another.
Cluny and Cîteaux both followed Benedict, and the Church honors saints from each; they heard the same Rule in different keys.
Jesus says to Martha, in the Douay-Rheims: "thou art careful, and art troubled about many things: But one thing is necessary."
Some readers hear the whole Cistercian plan in that sentence: plainer.

how: Cistercian monks and nuns, including the Trappists, still live by the Rule of Saint Benedict with manual work, silence and the hours of prayer, and their abbey churches are kept plain; some abbeys welcome guests for retreats.

games.q: you're a monk in a comfortable, respected monastery, but you think the Rule is being softened. what do you do?
o: leave with a few brothers to start a plainer house in a wild place.
games.why: Robert of Molesme left with a group of monks and founded the New Monastery at Cîteaux to keep the Rule more closely.

practice: Look around the room you're in and find one thing that crowds out what matters: a cluttered corner, an app you open without meaning to, a commitment kept out of habit.
Don't fix it; just see it plainly, and feel the space it would leave. If you pray, rest in Jesus's words to Martha: one thing is necessary.

wordCard.voice: Cistercian. A monk or nun of the way of life born at Cîteaux: the Rule of Benedict kept closely, in undyed wool, with plain churches and work of the hands. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: plainer. Less in the room can leave more room for what matters. See you tomorrow.
